back: The desire to put effort into work to achieve objectives; motivated staff raise output and quality and are less likely to leave.
Physiological, safety, social, esteem, self-actualisation (bottom to top); the lowest unmet need motivates.
Pay, working conditions, company policy, supervision, relationships and job security. If poor they cause dissatisfaction; if good they do not by themselves motivate.
Achievement, recognition, interesting work, responsibility and advancement; they produce satisfaction and extra effort.
Giving workers more responsibility, planning and decision-making in their jobs, to make the work itself more rewarding. Herzberg's main practical suggestion.
Enlargement adds more tasks of a similar level (less powerful); enrichment adds responsibility and control (more powerful).
The order is not fixed; needs differ between people and cultures; the levels overlap; hard to measure; not written for work.
Based on accountants and engineers; people credit themselves for success and blame others for failure; satisfaction does not always raise productivity; pay motivates some workers.

Maslow's lower levels are like Herzberg's hygiene factors; esteem and self-actualisation are like the motivators. Maslow says each need motivates until met; Herzberg says hygiene factors never motivate.
